inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,045 normalized lines. The paper develops two randomized extensions of Nyman-Beurling approximation: pNB averages squared error and can be derandomized to the classical criterion under a positive-probability support event, while gNB squares an averaged random Beurling function and needs moment plus coefficient-tail control to exclude zeta zeros. It also proves an RH-to-pNB direction for variables concentrating near reciprocal integers, identifies a probabilistic Muntz-transform representation for dilated variables, and applies the two mechanisms to exponential and Gamma laws. Prose, theorem structure, and proof strategy are recoverable; several displayed formulas have text-layer layout degradation and should be checked against the retained PDF before downstream use.

accepted_units.title: Mellin transform turns fractional-part dilation into zeta-weighted approximation
accepted_units.why_material: The displayed Mellin identity makes dilation multiplicative in the transform variable and turns density of fractional-part dilates in L2 into an RH-equivalent closure problem.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the transform identity, the continuous Nyman-Beurling theorem, and its finite-error formulation; lines 49-97 supply notation only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (1.1)-(1.3), whose mathematical content is readable but whose extracted fractions and braces should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: Reciprocal-integer dilates strengthen the criterion and expose quantitative distance
accepted_units.why_material: The move from arbitrary dilations to reciprocal integers yields the Baez-Duarte criterion, an orthogonal-projection distance formulation, conjectural rate information, and a link from approximation error to zero-free regions.
accepted_units.context_note: The failed L2 convergence of the naive Mobius partial sums motivates projection rather than literal series convergence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The criterion and distance discussion are prose-stable; the extracted summation and asymptotic formulas require notation-preserving rendering.

accepted_units.title: Muntz-transform criterion isolates compact support as the obstruction to analytic kernels
accepted_units.why_material: The general strong criterion reframes RH through approximation by dilated Muntz transforms and pinpoints why the known converse excludes noncompact analytic kernels, setting up the paper's controlled-tail repair.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the definition of the Muntz transform, the good-kernel theorem, its Mellin nonvanishing condition, and the stated open limitation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the extracted Muntz formula (1.6) and span statement (1.7); prose resolves their roles, but exact typography should be verified.

accepted_units.title: Two inequivalent placements of expectation define pNB and gNB
accepted_units.why_material: Placing expectation outside the squared Hilbert error versus inside each random fractional-part function creates distinct criteria, with Jensen's inequality giving pNB implies gNB.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the central representation fork for all subsequent arguments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The two nearly identical displayed definitions are vulnerable to extraction loss of distinguishing decorations; verify them against the PDF before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Random Beurling functions embed in a product Hilbert space with norm linear in the mean dilation
accepted_units.why_material: The product-space formulation turns random dilates into Hilbert vectors, suggests Gram-determinant structure, and proves that integrability of X suffices with an exact norm proportional to E[X].
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Fubini survival identity and scaling proof that make the random construction rigorous.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The norm constant and changes of variables are formula-dependent but recoverable; page-layout artifacts should be checked for exact notation.

accepted_units.title: Moment interpolation controls the L2 tail of a random Beurling function
accepted_units.why_material: The proposition converts an L2 moment of Z into a uniform decay estimate beyond a cutoff M, the reusable device later used for noncompact random dilates.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof combines scaling, Fubini, Cauchy-Schwarz, Markov, and monotonicity of moments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponent placement in the extracted inequality is fragile; retain the conceptual bound but verify exact powers from the source PDF.

accepted_units.title: A positive-probability bounded-support event derandomizes pNB into NB
accepted_units.why_material: Assumption P ensures a uniform positive chance that every sampled dilation lies in the classical interval; intersecting that event with a small-error event realizes one deterministic NB approximant and hence RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the exponential-law example and the full Markov-plus-intersection proof, which is the paper's explicit use of Erdos' probabilistic method.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The event definitions and probability inequalities are legible; displayed norm notation should be preserved exactly in a typeset representation.

accepted_units.title: The smallest sampled dilation limits probabilistic approximation quality
accepted_units.why_material: A deterministic lower bound at minimum scale transfers through the support event and Cauchy-Schwarz to show that pNB error cannot decay faster than permitted by the logarithmic size of the minimum dilation.
accepted_units.context_note: This complements the sufficient criterion with a geometric obstruction tied to how close the random family approaches zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact logarithms, indicators, and squared norms are formula-dependent and should be checked against the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: Concentration near reciprocal integers yields pNB equivalent to RH
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem packages mean matching, rapidly shrinking variance, and a nondegeneracy condition into a two-way criterion, explicitly connecting random perturbations to quantitative deterministic approximants.
accepted_units.context_note: Also records the two distinct uses of RH: explicit Baez-Duarte approximation and Lindelof growth on the critical line.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The square-root change of variables and Gamma parameters are extraction-sensitive; verify conditions (2.8)-(2.10) and the sample law.

accepted_units.title: Variance concentration recovers the positive-probability support condition
accepted_units.why_material: A union bound plus Chebyshev converts uniform small variance around reciprocal means into Assumption P, closing the easy direction from pNB to RH.
accepted_units.context_note: The first coordinate requires a separate nondegeneracy bound while all later coordinates are controlled collectively.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the extracted rate calculation, whose final decay order should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: Mellin-Plancherel frequency splitting stabilizes Mobius approximants under random perturbation
accepted_units.why_material: The proof compares randomized and deterministic fractional-part approximants, transfers their difference to the critical line, bounds low frequencies using concentration plus Lindelof, bounds high frequencies using integrability, and tunes the cutoff so both vanish.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the substantive RH-to-pNB mechanism and preserves the bounded Mobius coefficients needed for perturbation control.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly equation-dependent across (2.13)-(2.18); the prose establishes the split and tuning logic, but exact exponents and Mellin factors require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Vanishing L2 approximation excludes off-critical zeta zeros via a Mellin contradiction
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming an off-critical zero makes the Mellin transform of every approximation error equal a fixed nonzero target term, while splitting at t=1 and using L2 convergence forces that same integral to zero.
accepted_units.context_note: The tail estimate exploits the special linear form of fractional-part dilates and is the deterministic template for Theorem 8.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Mellin integral and tail identities are formula-sensitive, especially line-broken powers and sums; verify the exact display before training.

accepted_units.title: Admissible targets plus moment and coefficient-tail control suffice for gNB to imply RH
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 8 replaces the indicator target by any function with nonvanishing Mellin transform and controlled L2 tail, while explicitly states the moment and coefficient condition that compensate for unbounded random dilations.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the main noncompact-support sufficient criterion; its proof occupies the following units.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conditions T1, T2, (3.22), gNB, and C are equation-dependent and should be checked for exact quantifiers and exponents.

accepted_units.title: A moving Mellin cutoff separates approximation error from noncompact tails
accepted_units.why_material: At a hypothetical zeta zero the averaged approximation has a fixed nonzero Mellin value; choosing a threshold growing slowly enough makes the lower-range integral vanish by gNB error, reducing the contradiction to tail control.
accepted_units.context_note: The cutoff is selected from Dn tending to zero so that its weighted error also tends to zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transform identity and cutoff exponent depend on intact formula layout; verify exact powers in (3.24).

accepted_units.title: Rare large dilations are controlled by coefficient-weighted tail probability and moments
accepted_units.why_material: Splitting each expected fractional part according to whether Z exceeds the moving cutoff isolates a large-dilation term; Cauchy-Schwarz factors it into precisely condition C and the summable moment budget.
accepted_units.context_note: This explains why coefficient control is the price of allowing noncompact support.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definitions of A and B and estimates (3.25)-(3.28) are layout-fragile; the factorization logic is prose-recoverable but exact exponents need PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Bounded dilations are closed by target decay, gNB error, and the random-Beurling tail estimate
accepted_units.why_material: For dilations below the cutoff, the fractional part linearizes on the tail, reducing the remaining integral to a coefficient-weighted first moment; gNB, admissible-target decay, Proposition 2.2, and condition C then force it to zero.
accepted_units.context_note: Together with the previous unit this completes the generalized zero-exclusion contradiction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This span is densely formula-dependent and has degraded display ordering; exact inequalities (3.29)-(3.30) and cutoff powers require source-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Expected fractional parts are negative Muntz transforms of survival functions
accepted_units.why_material: Writing the survival function of X turns expectation of the random fractional part into a deterministic Muntz transform, furnishing a direct bridge between probability and the general strong criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof derives the identity first at unit scale and then by dilation, and explains when a continuous density produces a good kernel.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The series-integral rearrangement is recoverable, but the Muntz operator's extracted signs and scaling in (3.31)-(3.32) should be verified.

accepted_units.title: Deterministic strong approximation transfers RH to gNB for dilated random variables
accepted_units.why_material: Under RH, bounded deterministic Baez-Duarte coefficients approximate the indicator; the Muntz bridge transfers this to survival-function approximation by X/k, while a q-moment gives condition C through polynomial tail decay.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the converse construction matching Theorem 8 for a natural dilated family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theorem's gNB and C displays are clear in intent but exact norm and probability notation should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Exponential dilation and Gamma concentration instantiate different criterion routes
accepted_units.why_material: The examples separate a fixed-law dilation family handled through gNB/Muntz transfer from a triangular Gamma family handled through pNB concentration, and the implication map highlights that pNB can imply RH without condition C.
accepted_units.context_note: The final remarks flag unexplored correlation structure and simplified scalar products as possible further structure rather than proved parts of the criteria.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Gamma parameterization and implication diagram are substantially degraded by text extraction; verify them against the retained PDF before using the example quantitatively.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Derandomization versus averaging
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The placement of expectation determines the proof route: pNB supplies a good sample on a positive-probability support event, whereas gNB lacks that samplewise error and instead needs a Mellin argument with explicit tail hypotheses.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This comparison is internal to the paper's definitions and assumptions; it does not establish that either route is sharper for arbitrary random families.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Stability of a discrete RH criterion under concentrated randomization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Quantitative reciprocal-integer approximants remain effective after sufficiently small random perturbations because variance controls both admissible support and the low-frequency Mellin error, while a tuned frequency cutoff handles the tail.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The stated variance rate, mean matching, nondegeneracy, and RH-dependent Lindelof input are essential in the proved result; no generic robustness theorem is shown.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Coefficient control is a tail-compensation mechanism
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Removing compact support is made possible by splitting at a moving cutoff and pairing moment control of random dilates with coefficient-weighted rare-tail probabilities, rather than by ignoring the kernel tail.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper proves sufficiency under condition C; it does not claim C is necessary, and the pNB concentration example explicitly avoids it.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Survival functions bridge probabilistic dilation and Muntz approximation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The survival function converts an expected fractional-part dilation into a Muntz transform, so a deterministic strong approximation theorem can construct gNB approximants for X/k.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The transfer uses a continuous density to obtain a good kernel and a q-moment with q greater than one to verify coefficient-tail decay.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two model families expose complementary mechanisms
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Exponential dilates exercise the noncompact Muntz/gNB route, while triangular Gamma variables exercise concentration around reciprocal integers and the samplewise pNB route.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The extracted implication diagram and Gamma parameters need scan verification, and the paper leaves their correlation structure unexplored.
